key_insight: CutBackdoor shows that pre-trained VQA parameters can act as a backdoor trigger: they look benign on the full circuit but fail when the circuit is executed via qubit cutting.
engineering_relevance: This exposes circuit cutting as a new supply-chain security risk for near-term quantum workflows that must run beyond hardware qubit limits.
method: Poison the released VQA parameters rather than modifying the circuit.
Exploit CutQC-style circuit cutting as the deployment-time trigger.
Induce large reconstruction error on the cut path while preserving full-circuit validation performance.
evidence_signal: Across IBM backend experiments on VQE and VQD, the cut-path energy amplification reached about 1.3x to 2.9x over clean baselines while remaining stealthy on the full-circuit path.
watch_item: The attack depends on the victim using circuit cutting under resource limits, and Zero-Noise Extrapolation only partially reduces the effect.
paper_title: CutBackdoor: A Circuit Cut Triggered Backdoor Attack on Variational Quantum Algorithms
